general.temas: China’s diplomatic and trade relations, especially with the United States, and regional cooperation are recurring themes. Health, the environment and technological advances also feature. Xinhua stands out in particular for its coverage of COVID-19 and vaccination.
general.motivo_crispacion: Tensions stem from trade disputes between China and the United States, Chinese criticism of an initiative by Japan and the Philippines, and protests in the United States against attacks on Iran. Military aircraft movements and a case of alleged bribery in China are also mentioned. By contrast, there is abundant coverage of cooperation, health, agriculture and technology, without direct confrontation. The front pages refer to different dates, so they do not necessarily reflect the same day.

Diario del Pueblo.resumen:
- World Environment Day is the focus of several stories on ecological protection and Xi Jinping’s activities.
- Liu Guozhong calls for securing the summer harvest and preparing for autumn production; an agricultural census is announced for 2026.
- Han Zheng receives a US delegation for nongovernmental dialogue and emphasizes bilateral cooperation.
- Rules on military facilities and Party discipline are published; enforcement of the energy conservation law will also be reviewed.
- The front page covers arrangements for the university entrance exam, the heritage of Longjing tea and Xi’s activities in May.
Diario del Pueblo.motivo_populismo: Institutional language predominates, although expressions such as “the lifeline of fairness” and the question of how tea “conquers the heart of the world” add emotional emphasis; there is no discernible opposition between the people and the elites.
Diario del Pueblo.sesgo: The selection gives priority to the activities of the authorities and presents official initiatives from a favorable perspective. The environmental stories particularly emphasize Xi Jinping’s leadership.

Xinhua.resumen:
- The front page highlights the reopening of businesses and the recovery of activity following the optimization of COVID-19 measures.
- It covers the plan for a second booster dose and advice for older people and patients with cardiovascular conditions.
- It includes explanations of data on asymptomatic infections and the BQ.1 variant.
- It presents Xi Jinping’s activities and financial oversight measures linked to the 20th Party Congress.
- It also covers astronaut training, a piece on changes in China and the arrival of a cold wave.
Xinhua.motivo_populismo: The headlines are mostly informative, although some use curiosity-provoking or celebratory formulas, such as “what did they experience over 6, 10 and 12 years?” and “what’s new in China.”
Xinhua.sesgo: The selection prioritizes official decisions and explanations, as well as a positive presentation of changes in China and of its authorities. The texts provided contain hardly any critical or opposing perspectives.

Global Times.resumen:
- Analysts warn of the potential effects of a US plan concerning Chinese laboratories on supply chains and electronics costs.
- A South African commemoration addresses dignity and inclusive governance after apartheid.
- China announces a new rail timetable from July 1, including high-speed service between Beijing and Urumqi.
- A Chinese expert criticizes a Philippine claim about delimitation with Japan; another headline questions Yasukuni Shrine’s account of the Tokyo Trial.
- The front page also covers protests in the US, visits from Taiwan, sex education, artificial intelligence and China’s lunar plans.
Global Times.motivo_populismo: Most headlines are informative, but expressions such as “hidden motives,” “notorious inverted narrative” and “risk of more chaos” use accusatory or alarmist language.
Global Times.sesgo: The selection highlights the perspectives of Chinese experts and officials, with a positive emphasis on China’s advances and international role. Headlines about Japan, the Philippines and the United States take a critical approach in some cases.

CGTN.resumen:
- APEC is the focus of several stories about the arrival of Mexico’s president and a meeting of ambassadors and businesspeople in Shenzhen.
- Regional cooperation features in headlines about artificial intelligence, the Asia-Pacific region and the China-ASEAN summit.
- Eurasian companies explore opportunities in Chongqing, while Shenzhen stands out for its capacity for innovation.
- China announces the appointment of health professionals to educational institutions; another headline addresses the prudent use of antibiotics.
- The front page includes a call for closer China-US ties, statements on the Middle East and Africa, and the first flight of a Chinese solar-powered drone.
CGTN.motivo_populismo: An informative tone predominates, although “Shenzhen can make it happen in 20 minutes” is promotional and “the right side of history” introduces a simplistic moral opposition.
CGTN.sesgo: The selection favors a positive approach to China, its innovation and its international cooperation, featuring statements and perspectives from Chinese officials.

South China Morning Post.resumen:
- Trump’s Asia tour and his upcoming meeting with Xi dominate the front page, with attention to artificial intelligence and rare earths.
- The APEC summit brings together other diplomatic stories: China’s relations with Japan and Vietnam and tariff relief agreed with Canada.
- Kim Jong-un’s movements and the delegation accompanying Trump are examined.
- On military matters, Chinese air maneuvers and the tracking of two Russian aircraft near Taiwan are highlighted.
- China carries out a seabed mining test and accuses a former executive in its nuclear industry of bribery.
South China Morning Post.motivo_populismo: The headlines are mostly informative, although expressions such as “massive buildup” and the question about a greeting “without a smile” add drama; there is no discernible appeal to the people against the elites.
South China Morning Post.sesgo: The selection prioritizes diplomacy between leaders, trade tensions and security in Asia, with particular attention to China and the United States. Some interpretive headlines emphasize rivalry or diplomatic gestures.

opiniones.comunista:
I see a contradiction in the front pages: the protection of nature is championed while a Chinese mining test on the Pacific seabed is reported. I do not presume to know its effects, but I do demand that they be publicly assessed before it goes any further. The energy transition cannot become a new race to appropriate the commons.

An inspection of the enforcement of the energy conservation law is also announced, and food security is emphasized. For me, both tasks require public planning, the participation of workers and farmers, and collective control of resources. Big capital will seek profits; society needs clean air, food and accessible public services. A communist policy must be judged by its ability to put those needs above private profit.
opiniones.anarquista:
I read the news about protecting rivers and mountains and think that caring for nature is inseparable from caring for the lives of those who depend on it. But I am wary of presenting that task as a vision laid out from above: no party should monopolize decisions about territories inhabited by diverse communities. I would prefer those who work and care for them to be able to organize freely, share knowledge and decide together.

The Pacific seabed mining test also raises a question that should not be left exclusively in the hands of governments and companies: who decides what risks the sea should bear to obtain minerals? International cooperation matters, but I envision it as mutual support among peoples, with accessible information and real decision-making power, not as a division of power among hierarchies.
opiniones.liberal:
The environmental news reminds me that prosperity does not justify pollution. But protecting nature does not require the state to direct every activity: it requires clear rules, property rights and accountability for whoever causes harm. Farmers and businesspeople need freedom to innovate and conserve the resources on which their future depends.

I also view with concern the US plan to exclude Chinese laboratories from electronics testing. Raising trade barriers can make products more expensive and harm consumers and businesses. That is why I welcome China and Canada’s agreement to ease tariffs: trading freely is more beneficial than turning every exchange into a political dispute.

I prefer a limited state that enforces the rules without replacing individual decisions, and low taxes that leave people with more resources to start businesses and meet their responsibilities.
opiniones.extrema_derecha:
I see a lesson in the news that my country would do well to learn: sovereignty is not sustained by speeches. China considers food production strategic, regulates the construction of military facilities and seeks to preserve traditional techniques such as tea processing. I support those priorities: a nation that cannot feed and protect itself and pass on its culture ultimately becomes dependent on decisions made by others.

I also view trade and technology talks between major powers with caution. Cooperation can be useful, but handing over essential sectors in the name of globalization is irresponsible. And when the official press turns every initiative into a celebration of power, I demand more than ceremonies and slogans: verifiable results and accountability. Loyalty to the nation must not be confused with obedience to its elites.
opiniones.centro:
I find it encouraging that China and Canada have agreed on new trade concessions and that dialogue between China and the United States remains open. Competition between major powers will not disappear because of one meeting, but neither is it wise to turn every difference into a rupture. Businesses and workers need predictable rules, not a permanent escalation of barriers.

I also take seriously the Chinese press’s emphasis on the environment and food security. Protecting nature and securing harvests are not incompatible with growth: they require investment, effective regulation and support for rural communities. For me, good intentions must be accompanied by independent evaluation and public participation. I prefer gradual reforms subject to verifiable results to trusting that official announcements will suffice on their own.
